These results demonstrate that unified identity, safety, and placement management can convert structural redundancy in emerging agentic workflows into substantial serving-efficiency gains.
papers.title_zh: TwinHash：面向时间高效与能量高效智能体工作流的双侧对象身份管理
papers.abstract_zh: 智能体人工智能（AI）服务将大语言模型（LLM）生成与外部工具执行交织在一起，并日益依赖基于搜索的工作流，这些工作流会反复访问共享的推理状态和计算。这些模式在工具输出、LLM 响应和键值（KV）前缀之间造成大量冗余，然而现有服务系统主要优化共享提示前缀，而当相同请求产生不同输出时，朴素的以输入为键的缓存并不安全。我们提出 TwinHash，一种统一的对象管理架构，它为每个对象分配一个输入侧哈希键以识别重复请求，并分配一个输出侧内容指纹以验证和定位已存储状态，辅以类型特定的复用保护机制来保持正确性和响应多样性。一个软件对象身份表维护跨请求和轨迹的可复用对象，而一个硬件对象放置表跟踪它们在分层内存层级中的驻留情况，使得被逐出的状态可以被取回而不是重新计算。在七个智能体框架和五个基准套件中，复用更多地遵循工作流结构，而不是基准身份。在确定性工具读取反复出现的地方，TwinHash 可服务高达 81% 的工具输出；在基于搜索的框架中，可服务高达 92% 的 LLM 响应。从 DRAM 取回被逐出的 KV 前缀在 Qwen3-32B 上将 TTFT 最多降低 5.6 倍，并预计对更大的稠密模型带来更大收益。在基于搜索的框架下，相较于前缀缓存基线，TwinHash 将端到端实际耗时最多降低 87%，并将实测任务能耗最多降低 81%，同时每个键的服务上限控制自适应搜索中的质量—复用权衡。这些结果表明，统一的身份、安全性和放置管理能够将新兴智能体工作流中的结构性冗余转化为显著的服务效率提升。

papers.title: Memory as a Temporal Resource: Lifetime Contracts for Multi-Retention Systems
papers.summary: Computers move and rewrite data whose useful lifetimes range from inner-loop iterations to years, yet memory systems usually hide retention as a fixed physical property. We argue that required lifetime should become a first-class resource across algorithms, programming systems, controllers, and devices. Building on prior lifetime-aware placement, we propose an event-based validity contract that links application completion events to retention-class selection and renewal of protection. Applications would be enabled to express semantic contracts such as ``until this tile completes'' and the system will map data to homogeneous arrays engineered for ephemeral, epoch, or durable retention and preserve correctness through margins, ECC, refresh, migration, or recomputation. We present a trace-based simulator and FPGA prototype that exercises class migration.

papers.title: Forcing a Letter Suppresses Refusal: Mechanistic Evidence from WMDP
papers.summary: Safety benchmarks for large language models (LLMs) commonly use multiple-choice question (MCQ) format. However, prior studies documented that MCQ format reduces refusal rates, which may significantly affect the safety behavior of the model. We provide a first mechanistic explanation of this effect on the Weapons of Mass Destruction Proxy (WMDP) dataset across two models - Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen3-8B. First, we use the tuned lens technique to show that when processing MCQ the model commits to an answer-letter token very quickly, which is in contrast to the gradual refusal build-up in open-ended formats. Additionally, we observe that activations on the MCQ format lie roughly 3x further from the refusal direction, compared with their open-ended counterparts. Moreover, ablating the attention heads that carry the MCQ format answer increases the refusal, which is a direct evidence that the MCQ answer-selection competes with refusal. These findings indicate that MCQ safety scores primarily measure knowledge capabilities and do not assess the safety-mechanisms.
papers.title_zh: 强制给出一个字母会抑制拒绝：来自 WMDP 的机制证据
papers.abstract_zh: 大型语言模型（LLMs）的安全基准通常使用多项选择题（MCQ）格式。然而，已有研究记录到，MCQ 格式会降低拒绝率，这可能显著影响模型的安全行为。我们首次给出了这种效应在 Weapons of Mass Destruction Proxy（WMDP）数据集上跨两个模型——Llama-3.1-8B 和 Qwen3-8B——的机制性解释。首先，我们使用 tuned lens 技术表明，当处理 MCQ 时，模型会非常迅速地锁定到一个答案字母 token，这与开放式格式中拒绝的逐步累积形成对比。此外，我们观察到，与开放式对应情形相比，MCQ 格式上的激活值距离拒绝方向大约远 3 倍。而且，消融携带 MCQ 格式答案的注意力头会增加拒绝，这直接证明 MCQ 的答案选择与拒绝存在竞争。这些发现表明，MCQ 安全分数主要衡量知识能力，而并不评估安全机制。

papers.title: FinEvolveKG: Controlled and Attributable Prompt Evolution for Financial Knowledge Graph Construction
papers.summary: Financial institutions construct knowledge graphs (KGs) from shared SEC 10-Ks to serve risk analysis, portfolio management, and investment research, whose analytical needs differ. Extraction must adapt without fragmenting shared grounding, typing, and temporal rules. Hand-authored persona prompts and fine-tuning add cost. Weight-free prompt optimization offers an alternative, but unconstrained evolution of a monolithic prompt can rewrite shared rules alongside persona guidance, obscuring changes and complicating review. We introduce FinEvolveKG, a KG-construction harness separating reusable general and persona-policy blocks and mechanically confining GEPA, a reflective prompt optimizer, to the designated block. During persona adaptation, the approved general block remains byte-stable and every optimizer edit is localized to a separately versioned persona policy. A dual objective balances generic temporal-KG quality with persona-relevant facts, motifs, and multi-hop connectivity. We evaluate five mutation scopes on ticker-disjoint 10-K splits, with three seeds for the persona-conditioned arms (v3-v5) across three personas. On the three-seed mean, the complete two-stage block-constrained workflow (v4) improves over the frozen prompt baseline (v1) by 19.4-30.9% and over the tested unconstrained full-prompt workflow (v5) by 2.2-6.4%, leading v5 on both objective components and winning all nine paired-seed comparisons with the lowest seed variance in every persona. Without further optimization, v4 also exceeds v5 across all evaluated out-of-distribution (OOD) shifts. An SME audit supports using the generated triplets as ground truth; a blinded two-SME audit favors v4 over v5 in 70.1% of contrast-enriched judgments. These results show that mechanically attributable evolution can coexist with strong empirical performance, without attributing the gains causally to the boundary.

papers.title: Compression of Emotion in Language Model Representations
papers.summary: Large language models (LLMs) have been evaluated on their ability to identify emotions expressed in text and produce fluent emotional language. However, output predictions alone do not reveal how fine-grained emotion distinctions are organized internally. We study seven LLMs on GoEmotions, an English Reddit dataset annotated with 27 fine-grained emotion categories plus neutral. We compare model predictions and emotion-prompted final-token representations with the 28 GoEmotions categories and with coarser emotion-family and sentiment groupings. We find a consistent pattern of $\textit{overcompression}$ relative to the fine-grained GoEmotions taxonomy. Under the tested KMeans protocol, when we cluster their hidden representations without using emotion labels, the clearest split is into two groups that largely separate positive from negative emotion. Coarser emotion groupings are also recovered with fewer clusters than the full 28-category taxonomy. Yet linear probes retain substantial fine-grained predictive information. These results suggest that fine-grained emotion information remains accessible even though broader affective structure more strongly organizes the unsupervised geometry.
papers.title_zh: 语言模型表示中的情感压缩
papers.abstract_zh: 大型语言模型（LLMs）已在识别文本中表达的情感以及生成流畅的情感语言的能力上受到评估。然而，仅凭输出预测并不能揭示细粒度情感区分在内部是如何组织的。我们在 GoEmotions 上研究了七个 LLM，这是一个用 27 个细粒度情感类别加中性进行标注的英文 Reddit 数据集。我们将模型预测和情感提示下的最终 token 表示与 28 个 GoEmotions 类别以及更粗粒度的情感家族和情感倾向分组进行比较。我们发现了一个相对于细粒度 GoEmotions 分类法一致的 $\textit{overcompression}$ 模式。在所测试的 KMeans 协议下，当我们不使用情感标签对其隐藏表示进行聚类时，最清晰的分裂是分成两个在很大程度上将正性情感与负性情感分开的组。与完整的 28 类别分类法相比，更粗粒度的情感分组也能用更少的簇被恢复。然而，线性探针保留了相当多的细粒度预测信息。这些结果表明，尽管更宽泛的情感结构更强地组织了无监督几何结构，细粒度情感信息仍然可访问。

papers.title: Contextuality and Contradictions: Exploring Real-World Identifications of AI-Generated Writing
papers.summary: As AI-generated content spreads into nearly every domain of human interaction, practices and discourses of AI detection, both formal and informal, have become an everyday part of how people interact with text and with each other. In this paper, we explore the real-world practices and discourses of AI identification that have emerged in response to a shifting discursive landscape where the human provenance of a text can no longer be taken for granted. We pair qualitative coding with computational analysis of lexical change, grounded in linguistic anthropological perspectives on language and communication, to investigate AI identifications among English Wikipedia editors and students. We find that these identifications draw on a diversity of evidentiary types, from discrete textual features and judgments about content to circular sense-making claims and presumptions about the author's moral character, and that they are contradictory, dynamic, and contextually dependent. In practice, what often motivates an AI identification is not the presence of any specific textual element, but pragmatic infelicity: a perceived mismatch between the elements present and those deemed appropriate within the text's particular context. Consequently, real-world identifications of AI-generated writing do not merely neutrally point out the perceived presence of "AI-like" features, but can be leveraged as a discursive resource to maintain and define sociolinguistic norms: what can be said in a given context, what is appropriate, and, ultimately, what is human. Further, the design and implementation of systems and tools that treat AI-likeness as a context-free property of text may therefore inherit, and enforce at scale, the norms of whichever contexts they were trained on.

papers.title: RL-ATTACK: A Generalized Black-Box Adversarial Attack on Language Models via Reinforcement Learning
papers.summary: Large language models (LLMs) exhibit vulnerabilities to adversarial perturbations that can induce unintended responses. These vulnerabilities can be identified via intentional attacks and subsequently used to improve model safety. In black-box settings where gradients are inaccessible, existing methods tend to guess adversarial transformations using external knowledge, ignoring the information provided by the target model. To mitigate this, we propose a trainable black-box framework based on reinforcement learning, which learns from the target model to generate tailored adversarial transformations. We demonstrate that our approach achieves lower post-attack accuracy, greater query efficiency and better semantic preservation on both natural language inference and generative Q&A tasks. On natural language inference, it drives post-attack accuracy to 2% within 20 queries. Against generative language models, our trained attacker consistently achieves lower post-attack accuracy than the untrained attacker and wins in 4 out of 6 settings when compared to a strong optimization-based baseline. We further experiment with multiple reward designs and training settings, and we find that no design or setting is consistently dominant. Our code is available at https://github.com/taikunudel/RL-ATTACK.
papers.title_zh: RL-ATTACK：一种通过强化学习对语言模型实施的广义黑盒对抗攻击
papers.abstract_zh: 大型语言模型（LLMs）对对抗性扰动表现出脆弱性，这些扰动可以诱导出非预期响应。这些脆弱性可以通过有意攻击被识别出来，并随后用于改进模型安全性。在无法获取梯度的黑盒设置中，现有方法往往利用外部知识来猜测对抗性变换，而忽略了目标模型所提供的信息。为缓解这一问题，我们提出了一种基于强化学习的可训练黑盒框架，该框架从目标模型学习以生成量身定制的对抗性变换。我们证明，我们的方法在自然语言推理和生成式问答任务上均实现了更低的攻击后准确率、更高的查询效率和更好的语义保持。在自然语言推理上，它在20次查询内将攻击后准确率降至2%。针对生成式语言模型，我们训练后的攻击者始终比未训练的攻击者取得更低的攻击后准确率，并且在与强优化基线的比较中，在6个设置中的4个上胜出。我们进一步尝试了多种奖励设计和训练设置，并发现没有任何一种设计或设置始终占优。我们的代码可在 https://github.com/taikunudel/RL-ATTACK 获取。

papers.title: Structuring Survey Histories for LLM Digital Twins: A Controlled Study of Background, Decision Procedure, and Evaluation Profiles
papers.summary: LLM-based digital twins aim to predict how individuals would respond in new settings from representations of their prior responses. Existing evidence that compression of survey histories need not reduce predictive accuracy suggests that representation structure, rather than information volume alone, may be an important design choice. We study BDE, a fixed representation that organizes each respondent's survey history into Background, Decision procedure, and Evaluation. We evaluate it on Twin-2K-500 (Toubia et al., 2025) by predicting each respondent's held-out answers on 17 tasks. In a paired evaluation with 100 respondents, a fully inferred BDE profile improves overall accuracy over the raw survey transcript by 1.27 percentage points (pp) on gpt-5.4-nano (p < 0.01) and 1.19 pp on gpt-5.4-mini (p < 0.001). Three analyses then examine the schema, extraction depth, and component composition. Against a length-matched free-form profile written from the same transcript by the same extractor, BDE improves pricing accuracy on both simulators (2.15 pp on nano, p < 0.01; 1.38 pp on mini, p < 0.05), while its overall advantage is significant only on nano (1.05 pp, p < 0.05). Allowing deeper inference during extraction yields no statistically significant gain on either simulator. By contrast, adding Evaluation to a Background--Decision procedure profile improves overall accuracy by 1.44 pp on nano (p < 0.001) and 1.22 pp on mini (p < 0.001). These results indicate that the advantage over raw transcripts is not explained by compression or length alone, and attribute it primarily to profile composition rather than deeper extraction.

papers.title: Semantic Conditional Similarity (SCS): A Formal Mathematical Framework
papers.summary: Semantic Textual Similarity (STS) operates on document pairs, returning a single scalar per comparison. In a multi-document setting where several sources may have contributed to one or more targets, pairwise STS cannot disentangle each source's marginal semantic contribution from their shared vocabulary. In this paper, Semantic Conditional Similarity (SCS) is introduced as a conditional form of STS that computes similarity between two documents after eliminating semantic elements shared with a third via set-theoretic operations. SCS makes four contributions: 1) it introduces directionality, partitioning pairwise relations into lateral (inter-source) and vertical (source-to-target) classes; 2) conditioning induces role-dependent asymmetry by extending the comparison domain from unordered pairs to ordered, conditioned triples of a target, a reference, and a conditioning document; 3) SCS introduces inter-document conditioning by subtracting shared content from a third document, complementing the intra-document conditioning in recent C-STS work; and 4) the set-theoretic decomposition achieves threshold-free partitioning of shared and residual content, requiring no arbitrary similarity cutoff. Although developed for the $n \to 1$ configuration, the framework extends to $1 \to n$ via vertical role reversal and to $m \to n$ via independent composition of source- and target-side conditioning. With the established $1 \to 1$ case, these span the full spectrum of document cardinality. SCS scores should be interpreted ordinally, as rankings of marginal contributions rather than absolute measurements. The broader implication is that metric space axioms commonly assumed in similarity formalizations constrain expressiveness in role-differentiated multi-document settings, and that extending the domain to conditioned triples can recover information that pairwise-symmetric comparisons suppress.

papers.title: Guardrail Erosion in Domain Fine-Tuned Large Language Models: A Paired Audit of Knowledge-Centric Abstention in Biomedical LLMs
papers.summary: The number of domain fine-tuned models, particularly in the biomedical domain, is rapidly expanding. Fine-tuning promises high-performing models at a fraction of the cost of training a base model, but it can also produce unintended behavioral changes. Multiple studies have shown that safety guardrails can erode with fine-tuning, yet large-scale studies across model architectures, data mixtures, and fine-tuning methodologies remain limited. Where prior work in this space has studied value-centric refusal, this work focuses on knowledge-centric abstention. We audit 25 biomedical domain fine-tuned large language models against 11 paired base checkpoints on MedAbstain and ClinDet-Bench to evaluate the impact of fine-tuning on knowledge-centric abstention. We find that defined appropriate abstention measured by these benchmarks, already low in base models (median 8.3% on MedAbstain), falls further after fine-tuning (median 4.2%, decreasing in 21 of 25 pairs on MedAbstain), and that the magnitude and direction of change are heterogeneous across pairs. These results motivate fine-tuning methods that improve domain-specific capability while preserving appropriate caution.
papers.title_zh: 领域微调大语言模型中的护栏侵蚀：生物医学LLM中以知识为中心弃答的配对审计
papers.abstract_zh: 领域微调模型的数量，尤其是在生物医学领域，正在迅速扩张。微调有望以训练基础模型成本的一小部分获得高性能模型，但它也可能产生意想不到的行为变化。多项研究表明，安全护栏可能会随着微调而侵蚀，然而跨模型架构、数据混合和微调方法的大规模研究仍然有限。该领域先前的工作研究的是以价值为中心的拒绝，而本工作则聚焦于以知识为中心的弃答。我们在 MedAbstain 和 ClinDet-Bench 上审计了 25 个生物医学领域微调的大语言模型，对照 11 个配对的基座检查点，以评估微调对以知识为中心的弃答的影响。我们发现，由这些基准测量、被定义为适当的弃答在基座模型中已经很低（MedAbstain 上中位数为 8.3%），在微调后进一步下降（中位数为 4.2%，在 MedAbstain 上 25 对中有 21 对下降），并且变化的幅度和方向在各配对之间具有异质性。这些结果促使人们开发在提升领域特定能力的同时保留适当谨慎的微调方法。

papers.title: Richness Is Not Evenness: Ordered Renyi Crossings under Self-Training
papers.summary: Recursive self-training of language models, a setting studied in model collapse, can reduce vocabulary while making frequent words, mostly function words, less dominant. We fine-tune English GPT-2 on its own output for nine generations, vary the training-data sampling temperature, and measure every model with one fixed sampler. As training temperature rises, Renyi entropy changes turn from loss to gain at distinct temperatures: min-entropy first, then collision entropy, Shannon entropy and observed richness. Between the outer crossings, word types fall while the most-common word becomes less dominant. Untruncated training at T = 1 lies in this interval: at 13,000 words, generation 9 has 24% fewer types than generation 0 yet collision entropy is 0.91 bits higher. The ordering persists with a finer grid, different measurement samplers, a fixed word budget and five fresh training seeds. Min-entropy again crosses before richness in four further settings (in Hindi only at interpolated roots) and in 12 of 13 distinct measurements under eight text representations. Next-token identities and a categorical simulation isolate decoding and sampling effects; the crossing order remains empirical. Fine-tuning on human text can produce the same split while likelihood improves, and no single order's sign reliably identifies worse likelihood across the tested settings. We recommend reporting entropy profiles at stated budgets with an independent quality measure.

papers.title: From Procedures to Permissions: Learning Precise Subagent Authorization from Agent Skills
papers.summary: As language agents tackle increasingly complex tasks, they increasingly rely on multiple agents to coordinate specialized work, requiring decisions not only about what each subagent should do but also which tools and workspace resources it should access. Existing agent systems provide mechanisms for controlling tools and execution environments, but do not directly specify the resources required by each delegated subtask. Moreover, task outcomes and execution trajectories alone provide limited supervision for determining whether a subagent has received appropriate permissions. We observe that Agent Skills encode procedural knowledge describing the operations, tools, and files required at each step, providing a natural source of supervision for authorization. Building on this observation, we synthesize tasks and step-by-step procedures from Skills, execute them through subagent delegation in interactive environments, and use verified trajectories to construct training data for task execution and authorization. On ClawArena-Team, our method improves tool permission precision by 13.4 percentage points and workspace permission precision by 24.1 percentage points, while increasing overall task success by 11.6 percentage points for Qwen3.5-35B-A3B. On Terminal-Bench 2.1 and SkillsBench, our method remains competitive with existing agent data synthesis approaches. These results show that the procedural knowledge embedded in Agent Skills provides a source of supervision for precise subagent orchestration that task outcomes alone cannot provide.

papers.title: On the Incompleteness of do-calculus for Universal Identifiability
papers.summary: We study the problem of causal effect identification from an arbitrary set of observational and/or interventional distributions, which we call Universal Identifiability (uID). The uID problem generalizes existing classical identifiability (ID) and general identifiability (gID) problems, which considered the identification problem from either mere observational distributions or a specific type of interventional distributions. Prior research has established graphical criteria to determine when a causal effect is identifiable in ID and gID problems. Moreover, algorithms that leverage do-calculus and basic probability manipulations have been proposed to compute these effects. Consequently, it has been shown that do-calculus is both sound and complete in these problems. Despite these well-established results, a formal definition of what it means for the do-calculus to be complete does not exist. We propose a rigorous formalization for the completeness of the do-calculus and show that the completeness results in previous work remain valid. However, for more general problems, such as uID, the rules of do-calculus are no longer complete. This is perhaps the reason why the uID problem has remained open thus far.

papers.title: Using an LLM to Tackle Difficult Cases in NER for Nepali Tweets
papers.summary: Named entity recognition (NER) is challenging for social media data in a low-resource language. LLMs often lag behind pretrained language models (PLMs) in NER performance, but they show promise in handling cases that PLMs struggle with. Using a dataset of Nepali tweets, we split the test set into "easy" and "hard" cases using token probabilities from a fine-tuned pretrained language model (PLM). We then evaluate an LLM on the hard test cases using 16 different prompt configurations. We find that selecting examples based on semantic similarity and increasing the number of examples improves F1 score by almost 10 points from the baseline configuration. Although the LLM underperforms the PLM on the full and easy test sets, it surpasses the PLM on the hard test set, resulting in an improved score when the two models are combined.

papers.title: Beyond Truncation? Entailment-Licensed Elision and the Limits of Semantic Preservation in LLM Decoding
papers.summary: Instruction-tuned large language models (LLMs) answer at greater length than a request needs. We ask whether a training-free controller inside the decoding loop can remove that surplus while preserving content, judged against the simplest possible baseline: truncating the model's own answer to the same length. An entropy-gated logits processor removes 25.5-34.9% of tokens on MT-Bench development questions and 19.9-34.2% on a sealed test split within pre-registered BERTScore non-inferiority margins, yet we prove and confirm by audit that its output is always a prefix of the unmodified answer: the saving is truncation. A survey of 23 training-free mechanism families finds none that selects content better than truncation without oracle labels. We therefore introduce Entailment-Licensed In-Decoding Elision (ELIDE), which, at each sentence boundary, withholds a span from the reader only when a natural-language inference model judges it entailed by the text already shown, while leaving the model's generation unchanged. ELIDE beats matched-length truncation on three model families, but reading 936 of its elisions on 670 public prompts shows that 59% harm the answer, a failure that no automatic measure detects. Scoping the licence to its discourse unit reduces the harmful share to about one elision in ten on two fresh tests.
papers.title_zh: 超越截断？蕴含许可的省略与 LLM 解码中语义保持的限度
papers.abstract_zh: 指令微调的大语言模型（LLM）给出的回答长度超过请求所需。我们探讨解码循环内一个无需训练的控制器能否在保留内容的同时去除这种冗余，并以最简单的基线——将模型自身回答截断到相同长度——作为评判标准。一个熵门控 logits 处理器在 MT-Bench 开发问题上移除了 25.5–34.9% 的 token，在密封测试划分上移除了 19.9–34.2% 的 token，且处于预先注册的 BERTScore 非劣效性边界内；然而我们证明并通过审计确认，其输出始终是未修改回答的一个前缀：所节省的只是截断。对 23 个无需训练的机制族进行的综述发现，在没有 oracle 标签的情况下，没有一个机制族能比截断更好地选择内容。因此，我们引入蕴含许可的解码中省略（Entailment-Licensed In-Decoding Elision，ELIDE）：它在每个句子边界处，仅当自然语言推理模型判定某个片段已被此前展示的文本所蕴含时，才不向读者展示该片段，同时保持模型的生成不变。ELIDE 在三个模型族上优于等长截断，但在 670 个公开提示上阅读其 936 处省略后显示，59% 的省略损害了回答，而这种失败没有任何自动指标能够检测到。将许可范围限定到其话语单元后，在两个新的测试上，有害省略所占比例降至约每十处省略中有一处。

papers.title: Language, Not Code Abstraction: Natural-language Training Shapes Brain-aligned Geometry
papers.summary: Code-trained language models produce positive brain scores, which raises the question of whether abstract structure learned from programming languages can substitute for natural-language training. We trained 25 GPT-2-small models on TinyStories, Python, C functions, x86-64 assembly, and the corresponding machine code, and scored them using a shared tokenizer and encoding procedure against matched random-weight models. On Pereira-243 and Tuckute2024, TinyStories exceeds the mean of the four code models by $Δr = 0.053$ and $0.059$ (Holm-corrected $p<0.001$), while code training leaves alignment near the random-weight level. The language advantage is benchmark-specific: Blank2014 shows no corrected language-code difference, and Fedorenko2016 shows no language benefit. Geometry tracks the encoding result on Pereira-243: TinyStories seeds converge on the most similar representations, and its fit-free correspondence with neural dissimilarity peaks at $ρ= 0.14$, twice the code and random-weight levels. Binary-trained models have about three effective dimensions, so seed agreement alone does not imply neural correspondence. Updating only the embedding matrix on English improves mean-over-depth alignment for every code model more than an equal update on its own corpus. Within this architecture and training setup, natural-language training produces a distinct representational geometry with closer neural correspondence on Pereira-243

papers.title: Failure Profiling and Reachable Trajectory Selection for Reasoning Distillation
papers.summary: Training smaller language models on reasoning solutions generated by a larger teacher model is the prevailing approach for transferring mathematical reasoning capabilities. However, the student tends to overfit the output distribution of the teacher and generalizes poorly when its own behavior at inference time deviates from the training data. Recent methods attempt to bridge this gap by incorporating error data, yet the corrective trajectories still reflect the reasoning patterns of the teacher, which the student cannot reliably reproduce, leaving the distribution mismatch largely unresolved. We propose a method, Failure Profiling and Reachable Trajectory Selection (FPRT), built on the insight that effective training data should be jointly determined by what the student fails on and what it can realistically learn. Our method first profiles the failure behavior of the student on each problem through repeated sampling, characterizing it in terms of error rate and error consistency to reveal qualitatively distinct failure modes. Each mode demands a fundamentally different training signal. The diagnosed mode then guides candidate generation from the teacher via distinct prompting strategies tailored to each failure type. Among the correct candidates, our method selects the one whose initial reasoning steps after the point of divergence are most reproducible by the student. These first corrective steps constitute the primary bottleneck, while the remaining steps follow an already corrected context and can therefore be continued more readily. This contrasts with standard reranking approaches, which score the trajectory as a whole and thereby dilute the signal at the critical reasoning transition. Experiments demonstrate that our method achieves the SOTA performance across the five benchmarks on both student backbones.

papers.title: Does Reasoning Improve Psychological Depth in Large Language Models?
papers.summary: Benchmark gains from reasoning-enhanced large language models encourage the assumption that these models should broadly perform better on complex generative tasks, but this remains underexplored in open-ended, creative domains shaped by nuances of reader experience. We tested this assumption through the lens of psychological depth in short stories. We compared DeepSeek-R1 vs. DeepSeek-V3, our closest available contrast for reasoning-oriented post-training, and GPT-5 vs. GPT-4o, through 60 blinded pairwise evaluations in which seven human annotators and an ensemble LLM-as-a-Judge rated prompt-matched story outputs. Human evaluations showed no universal reasoning advantage: GPT-5 was slightly preferred over GPT-4o (60.0-62.9% across two reasoning-effort settings), whereas DeepSeek-R1 fell behind DeepSeek-V3 (42.9%). Although this pattern was marked by low inter-annotator agreement (Krippendorff's $α= 0.070$), our annotation-quality checks suggested genuine evaluative subjectivity, plausibly reflecting distinct annotator decision schemes rather than annotation failure. In contrast, the LLM-as-a-Judge showed a strong pro-reasoning bias (98.3% of pairs vs. 55.2% of human votes), consistent across its five configurations and partly tracking sentence length. These findings suggest that, at the frontier, reasoning-related quality differences are small enough to be dominated by reader subjectivity, and that LLM-as-a-Judge evaluators can obscure this subjectivity in nuanced creative-generation tasks.
papers.title_zh: 推理是否提升大语言模型的心理深度？
papers.abstract_zh: 推理增强型大语言模型在基准测试上的收益，促使人们假设这些模型应在复杂生成任务上广泛表现更好，但这一假设在由读者体验细微差异塑造的开放式、创造性领域中仍未得到充分探索。我们通过短篇小说的心理深度这一视角检验了这一假设。我们比较了 DeepSeek-R1 与 DeepSeek-V3，这是我们在面向推理的后训练方面可用的最接近对比，并比较了 GPT-5 与 GPT-4o，通过 60 次盲法成对评估，由七名人类标注者和一个集成式 LLM-as-a-Judge 对提示匹配的故事输出进行评分。人类评估未显示出普遍的推理优势：GPT-5 相较 GPT-4o 略受偏好（在两种推理努力设置下分别为 60.0-62.9%），而 DeepSeek-R1 落后于 DeepSeek-V3（42.9%）。尽管这一模式以较低的标注者间一致性为特征（Krippendorff's $α= 0.070$），我们的标注质量检查表明这属于真实的评价主观性， plausible地反映了不同的标注者决策方案，而非标注失败。相比之下，LLM-as-a-Judge 表现出强烈的偏向推理的偏差（成对中 98.3% 对 人类投票的 55.2%），在其五种配置中保持一致，并部分与句子长度相关。这些发现表明，在前沿水平上，与推理相关的质量差异小到足以被读者主观性所主导，并且 LLM-as-a-Judge 评估器可能在细微的创造性生成任务中掩盖这种主观性。

papers.title: The Invisible Gap: Romanized Indic Generation Fails Where Automatic Metrics Succeed
papers.summary: Hundreds of millions of Indians communicate with digital systems in romanized Latin characters -- typing "aap kaise hain" rather than native script -- yet romanized Indic generation is absent from NLP benchmarks and evaluation frameworks. We demonstrate that automatic metrics (BGE-M3, BERTScore) systematically misrepresent the quality of romanized Hindi, Telugu, and Kannada generation. We evaluate four LLMs (Claude Opus 4.8, GPT-5.5, Gemini 2.5-flash, Qwen3.5-35B) on 142 OpenAssistant query-response pairs. On a 72-response diagnostic subset, native speakers rate GPT-5.5 1.43 points higher than Claude Opus 4.8 on a 12-point rubric, whereas their full-dataset BGE-M3 means differ by only 0.004. Two distinct model-specific failure modes emerge: Gemini produces script spillage (16.9% of Telugu responses leak native script), while Qwen collapses to English-only output (16.2% of Kannada responses). We introduce a failure-aware evaluation policy that assigns zero to empty outputs, script-corrupted responses, and instruction collapses -- revealing failures metrics alone cannot detect. Our results show that evaluating romanized Indic generation requires a coordinated bundle: semantic similarity, script compliance, failure coverage, and native-speaker acceptability.

papers.title: MARS: Training Multilingual Search Agents for Retriever-Free Evidence Acquisition
papers.summary: Existing multilingual retrieval-augmented generation relies heavily on learned retrievers and similarity-based ranking from multilingual collections, which are vulnerable to cross-lingual retrieval errors and indexing overhead. In this paper, we explore retriever-free multilingual search, where the model directly interacts with raw corpora through executable shell commands. This paradigm shifts the bottleneck to multilingual search action generation, where exact search is sensitive to entity surface forms and outcome-only supervision provides limited guidance for multi-turn search. To address these challenges, we propose MARS, a multilingual search agent in direct corpus interaction (DCI) with reinforcement learning (RL). MARS introduces corpus-native entity grounding to recover reliable lexical anchors from corpus evidence, mitigating failure to retrieve evidence. Meanwhile, we present a redundancy-aware search reward to encourage concise and effective search trajectories, addressing training collapse in RL of multilingual scenarios. Experiments show that \ours~consistently outperforms strong retrieval-based and DCI baselines, while demonstrating robust cross-lingual generalization and substantially reducing redundant corpus interactions.

papers.title: AlienBench: A Benchmark of Structural Novelty in Language Model Outputs
papers.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for creative tasks such as writing, design, and idea generation. For these uses, it matters whether a model's ideas depart from familiar examples or stay close to them. Novelty is one standard measure of creativity, and current creativity evaluations ask human experts or LLM judges to rate how novel an output is. However, these ratings have no fixed reference for what counts as novel (or, in other terms, departure from the familiar). Measuring this departure requires a task with known familiar defaults. The structured imagination task from cognitive psychology is such a task. In this creativity test, people imagine a creature from another planet. The departure from features of Earth animals, such as bilateral symmetry and legs as mode of locomotion, is used as measure of creativity. We introduce AlienBench, a benchmark that adapts the structured imagination task to language models. Models describe alien creatures, and a panel of three LLM judges extracts ten biological features from the description and labels them as either Earth-typical or a departure. The sum of feature departures is the score of a description, from 0 to 10. Each model describes alien creatures under six prompt conditions that vary the framing of the task and the planetary environment. Each model generates 30 descriptions per condition (180 in total), and its overall score is the mean across these descriptions. We evaluate 10 language models, from frontier to open-weight models. Overall scores range from 3.28 (GPT-6 Luna) to 6.55 (Ministral 3 14B). Interestingly, open-weight models score higher than proprietary models in this task (5.40 vs. 4.58). Under the baseline prompt, the models depart from Earth defaults more often on average than 100 human participants on every feature. We release all prompts, generations, judge outputs, and scores.
papers.title_zh: AlienBench：语言模型输出中结构新颖性的基准
papers.abstract_zh: 大语言模型（LLMs）正越来越多地被用于写作、设计和创意生成等创造性任务。在这些用途中，模型的想法是偏离熟悉的示例还是与之接近，这一点很重要。新颖性是创造力的一种标准度量，而当前的创造力评估让人类专家或LLM评判者对一个输出的新颖程度进行评分。然而，这些评分对于什么算作新颖（或者换句话说，对熟悉事物的偏离）没有固定的参照。测量这种偏离需要一个具有已知熟悉默认项的任务。认知心理学中的结构化想象任务就是这样一种任务。在这项创造力测试中，人们想象一种来自另一颗行星的生物。与地球动物特征（例如两侧对称和以腿作为运动方式）的偏离被用作创造力的度量。我们提出AlienBench，这是一个将结构化想象任务适配到语言模型的基准。模型描述外星生物，由一个由三个LLM评判者组成的小组从描述中提取十个生物特征，并将其标记为地球典型特征或偏离。特征偏离的总和是一个描述的得分，范围为0到10。每个模型在六种提示条件下描述外星生物，这些条件改变任务的框架和行星环境。每个模型在每种条件下生成30个描述（总共180个），其总体得分是这些描述的平均值。我们评估了10个语言模型，从前沿模型到开放权重模型。总体得分范围从3.28（GPT-6 Luna）到6.55（Ministral 3 14B）。有趣的是，在这项任务中，开放权重模型的得分高于专有模型（5.40 对 4.58）。在基线提示下，模型在每一个特征上平均比100名人类参与者更频繁地偏离地球默认项。我们发布所有提示、生成结果、评判者输出和得分。

papers.title: PhoPunct: A Large-Scale Benchmark of Transformer Architectures for Vietnamese Punctuation Restoration
papers.summary: Vietnamese punctuation restoration is often evaluated on relatively small benchmarks, limiting conclusions about how architectural choices scale with data volume. We present a controlled benchmark on News and Novels corpora containing 22.1 million labeled tokens (19.9M News and 2.2M Novels). We evaluate 17 architectures formed from four pretrained Transformer backbones and optional bidirectional long short-term memory (Bi-LSTM) and conditional random field (CRF) layers, together with a PhoBERT-large-Bi-LSTM-CRF model, PhoPunct. Every model is trained for eight epochs with the same learning rate and without architecture-specific tuning. Under this fixed budget, adding Bi-LSTM and CRF layers does not reliably improve macro F1: in seven of eight matched domain-backbone comparisons, a plain Transformer classifier matches or outperforms its Bi-LSTM-CRF counterpart. PhoPunct obtains the best News result (61.35), whereas XLM-R with a CRF obtains the best Novels result (50.18), exceeding PhoPunct (48.97). These results show that the value of recurrent and structured-prediction heads depends on their optimization regime and motivate explicit separation between architectural improvements and improvements due to architecture-specific tuning. Our source code is available at: https://github.com/aisia-research-lab/PhoPunct

papers.title: Calibrated concept profiles: making the reading of a model's neurons a measurement
papers.summary: Interpretability has largely moved from reading a model's neurons directly to reading a second model trained on the first: a probe, a sparse autoencoder, a crosscoder. The move answered real faults -- mixed meanings, thresholds without a unit, readings that did not transfer from one study to the next -- but gave up what a direct reading alone provides: nothing trained in between, the neurons themselves named, and a reading that can be repeated and compared. Here the direct reading is made a measurement. A neuron's activation varies with the prompt, so its reading is a distribution over a population of stimuli. We declare that population: every factor around a target construct is drawn at its rate in a reference corpus and logged. From the declared distribution we generate a battery of prompts, and draw it twice. From the battery we compute the calibrated concept profile, one number per neuron, stated in units of the neuron's own spread on ordinary input; the two draws give every number a noise unit. Before the profile is read, a fixed set of checks licenses the battery on the model, and the smallest change the profile can resolve across training checkpoints is measured. Realised for Python on OpenCoder-1.5B and followed across checkpoints spanning two trillion training tokens, the profile gives what the alternatives do not report: a unit on every number, a chance level for every comparison, and which neurons carry a construct at every checkpoint. The battery, the code and the data behind every result are released.

papers.title: Representational drift in a code model: behaviour settles, which neurons carry it does not
papers.summary: In neuroscience, representational drift is a change in which neurons carry a representation while behaviour stays the same; we measure its analogue in OpenCoder-1.5B during pretraining, for 169 Python constructs over two trillion tokens at a constant learning rate, with a noise unit on every change, at checkpoints as close as 1,000 training steps. For 16 of the 169, those whose grammar fixes a next token, the loss at those positions reaches its floor within the first 4% of training, while the model's reliance on the neurons carrying them grows to the end: removing them costs 0.06, 0.25 and 0.40 nats more than removing a random set, at 4 billion, 84 billion and 2 trillion tokens. Which neurons carry a construct never settles: for all 169 the carrier set is still changing at the last checkpoint, and an abrupt settling at any date from 84 billion to 1.5 trillion tokens, or a gradual one before 500 billion, would have been detected in 99% of injected cases. The set measured at 84 billion tokens, removed at the end, cannot be separated from a random set, so the function is carried by whichever neurons are current. Up close the change is a persisting pool and a changing sample: a neuron that leaves a construct's set returns at three times the rate of a matched neuron, and no set reassembles. The hypothesis we fixed in advance, that the carriers settle, is refuted; we discuss candidate causes and name the experiment that would separate them.

papers.title: Khmer PFGen-Bench: Building a Judge-Free Benchmark for Open-Ended Generation in a Low-Resource Language
papers.summary: Benchmarks for open-ended generation often rely on large language model (LLM) judges, whose reliability in low-resource languages is uncertain. We introduce Khmer PFGen-Bench, to our knowledge the first judge-free benchmark for multi-sentence answers to questions composed directly in Khmer, a low-resource language. Khmer PFGen-Bench adapts the scorer of PFGen-Bench, a benchmark for Japanese that scores responses with keyword rules and n-gram statistics from LLM-generated references. This scoring requires references that are both valid and varied, which LLMs may not produce in Khmer, so we examine how to build such references. We find that post-trained models can give more valid but less varied references than their base variants, and that mixing model families increases variety for the same number of references. Using references from post-trained models in nine families, the benchmark yields model rankings that are stable across reference sets and consistent with a native speaker's ratings. These findings offer guidance for building judge-free benchmarks in other low-resource languages.
papers.title_zh: Khmer PFGen-Bench：构建面向低资源语言开放式生成的免评判基准
papers.abstract_zh: 开放式生成的基准往往依赖大语言模型（LLM）评判器，而其在低资源语言中的可靠性尚不确定。我们提出 Khmer PFGen-Bench，据我们所知，这是首个针对直接用高棉语（一种低资源语言）编写的问题的多句答案的免评判基准。Khmer PFGen-Bench 改编了 PFGen-Bench 的评分器；PFGen-Bench 是一个面向日语的基准，它利用关键词规则和来自 LLM 生成参考文本的 n-gram 统计对回答进行评分。这种评分要求参考文本既有效又多样，而 LLM 在高棉语中可能无法生成这样的参考文本，因此我们考察如何构建此类参考文本。我们发现，经过后训练的模型相比其基础版本能够给出更有效但多样性更低的参考文本，并且在参考文本数量相同时，混合不同模型家族可以提高多样性。使用来自九个模型家族的后训练模型所生成的参考文本，该基准产生的模型排名在不同参考集之间保持稳定，并与一位母语者的评分一致。这些发现为在其他低资源语言中构建免评判基准提供了指导。

papers.title: KLEAR: Knowledge-Matched LLM Evaluation in Korean across Application Requirements via Controlled Benchmark Transformation
papers.summary: Existing Korean benchmarks for Large Language Models (LLMs) evaluate performance across diverse knowledge domains, but their accuracy scores cannot distinguish whether incorrect responses arise from a lack of required knowledge or a failure to apply that knowledge correctly. Our analysis of existing Korean benchmarks reveals that most questions can be answered through factual recall alone, while those demanding greater application also differ in required knowledge, making it difficult to isolate application ability. To address this, we introduce KLEAR, a framework that constructs knowledge-matched contrasts by varying application demand while preserving the required knowledge. During construction, KLEAR identifies the knowledge underlying each source question as an explicit anchor bundle to guide generation of questions requiring more complex application. Generated candidates then undergo automated and human validation, with iterative revision based on evaluation feedback. Experiments demonstrate that the resulting knowledge-matched sets largely satisfy the intended constraints, enabling controlled evaluation across diverse LLMs. These evaluations reveal that increasing application demand exposes failures that persist even when the required knowledge is provided.
papers.title_zh: KLEAR：通过受控基准转换实现跨应用需求的韩语知识匹配LLM评估
papers.abstract_zh: 现有面向大语言模型（LLMs）的韩语基准评估跨多样知识领域的性能，但其准确率分数无法区分错误回答是源于缺乏所需知识，还是源于未能正确应用该知识。我们对现有韩语基准的分析表明，大多数问题仅通过事实回忆即可回答，而那些要求更高应用能力的问题在所需知识上也存在差异，从而难以隔离出应用能力。为解决这一问题，我们提出KLEAR，一个通过改变应用需求同时保持所需知识不变来构建知识匹配对照的框架。在构建过程中，KLEAR将每个源问题背后的知识识别为显式锚点束，以指导生成需要更复杂应用的问题。生成的候选问题随后经过自动化和人工验证，并基于评估反馈进行迭代修订。实验表明，所得的知识匹配集合在很大程度上满足预期约束，从而能够在多样LLMs上进行受控评估。这些评估揭示，提高应用需求会暴露出即使提供了所需知识仍持续存在的失败。

papers.title: DUET: Dual-Sparse Inference for Block Diffusion Language Models
papers.summary: Diffusion language models (DLMs) enable parallel token generation through iterative denoising, yet their inference remains costly due to repeated attention over a growing historical prefix and repeated processing of the entire current generation block. Historical attention becomes increasingly expensive as generation progresses, while all current-block positions are propagated through the Transformer at every denoising step even though only a small fraction are typically resolved at that step. In this paper, we introduce Duet, a training-free dual-sparse inference framework that addresses these challenges through prefix Key-Value (KV) sparsity and early query sparsity, respectively. Specifically, Duet exploits the concentration and cross-step stability of historical attention within each generation block to construct a compact historical KV subset that is reused across denoising steps. For query sparsity, Duet predicts update positions from shallow representations and propagates only the corresponding queries through the suffix Transformer layers, avoiding deep computation at positions unlikely to be updated in the current step. Experiments show that Duet maintains competitive accuracy while achieving 1.34$\times$/2.83$\times$ end-to-end/per-step speedups on LLaDA2.1-mini and 2.41$\times$/4.72$\times$ on SDAR-8B-Chat-b32 at a 32K context length.
papers.title_zh: DUET：面向块扩散语言模型的双稀疏推理
papers.abstract_zh: 扩散语言模型（DLMs）通过迭代去噪实现并行 token 生成，然而由于对不断增长的历史前缀的重复注意力以及对整个当前生成块的重复处理，其推理仍然代价高昂。随着生成推进，历史注意力变得越来越昂贵；而在每个去噪步骤中，当前块的所有位置都会通过 Transformer 传播，尽管通常只有一小部分会在该步骤被确定。本文提出 Duet，一种无需训练的双稀疏推理框架，分别通过前缀键值（KV）稀疏性和早期查询稀疏性来应对这些挑战。具体而言，Duet 利用每个生成块内历史注意力的集中性和跨步骤稳定性，构建一个紧凑的历史 KV 子集，并在去噪步骤间复用。对于查询稀疏性，Duet 从浅层表示预测更新位置，并仅将相应的查询传播通过后缀 Transformer 层，避免在当前步骤中不太可能被更新的位置进行深层计算。实验表明，Duet 保持有竞争力的准确率，同时在 32K 上下文长度下，在 LLaDA2.1-mini 上实现 1.34$\times$/2.83$\times$ 的端到端/每步加速，在 SDAR-8B-Chat-b32 上实现 2.41$\times$/4.72$\times$ 的加速。

papers.title: Multilingual Artificial Datasets for AI-Driven Cardiology: the CliTe and ParaCliTe corpora
papers.summary: Background and Aims. Comparable, multilingual, validated cardiology corpora are critical to advance trustworthy natural language processing (NLP) models for cardiology but such resources are scarce due to privacy concerns. This study aimed to cover this gap by presenting suitable artificial corpus creation guidelines and by releasing 3 multilanguage corpora. Methods. Following purpose-specific publicly-available corpus construction guidelines, cardiologists from 7 European hospitals generated artificial clinical records in Czech, Dutch, English, Italian, Romanian, Spanish and Swedish, ensuring clinical diversity and sex balance, resulting in the CliTe corpus. A CliTe subset underwent a multi-stage manual translation into the other 6 languages, resulting in the parallel ParaCliTe corpus, while the remaining reports were automatically translated, constituting ParaCliTe Silver. Results. CliTe is a collection of 699 artificial cardiology reports, mostly outpatient notes (340 documents), discharge reports (263), and inpatient notes (89), describing fictional patients with ischaemic heart disease (199 patients), heart failure (188), and valvular disease (79), among others. ParaCliTe contains reports from 94 fictitious patients, each available in seven languages with sentence-level alignment, resulting in 658 documents. The corpus mainly comprises discharge reports (322 documents), and outpatient (196) and inpatient (140) notes, describing patients with heart failure (399 documents), ischaemic heart disease (287), and valvular disease (238). Empirical results illustrate the utility of ParaCliTe and highlight the limitations of state-of-the-art NLP models adapted to the cardiology domain. Conclusions. The creation of multilingual, equitable and realistic corpora of artificial patients capable of strengthening NLP performance for cardiology is feasible when supported by detailed guidelines.

papers.title: Asymmetric Correspondence Learning for Lexical and Style Embeddings: Interpreting Latent Space via Acoustic Features
papers.summary: Self-supervised speech embeddings jointly encode lexical, speaker, and prosodic information, complicating feature isolation. We introduce Asymmetric Correspondence Learning (ACL), distilling HuBERT features into separate Acoustic Word Embeddings (AWEs) and Acoustic Style Embeddings (ASEs) via a split-latent correspondence bottleneck. Through probing and clustering evaluations on single-word utterances, we demonstrate that substantial variance from extrinsic sources remains encoded within each latent space, despite linear probing indicating the information has been stripped. Whilst the AWE space exhibits cohesive lexical clustering (AP$\approx$0.90, Fisher$\approx$6.28), linear probing on the ASE space achieves 97.9\% speaker accuracy across a diffuse topology (Fisher$\approx$1.01), yet preserves substantial lexical variance (Fisher$\approx$0.86) that remains linearly unrecoverable (0.17\%). To explain these findings, we apply group-level permutation feature importance over eGeMAPS acoustic features, finding that AWEs partition by vocal tract filters and ASEs by $F_0$ dynamics. These findings suggest that standard diagnostic benchmarks may be insufficient for verifying feature isolation, as substantial speech structure can be retained even when it remains entirely hidden from probes.

papers.title: Syn2DRE: Synergistic Dual Teacher-Student Framework for Document-level Relation Extraction
papers.summary: Document-level Relation Extraction (DocRE) aims to identify relations between entities across a document but typically relies on costly large-scale annotations. While pseudo-labelling enables the use of low-quality data, existing methods often suffer from inefficiency and confirmation bias. To address these challenges, we propose Syn2DRE, a semi-supervised framework that combines self-supervised learning with cross-supervision in a lightweight teacher-student architecture to produce more reliable pseudo-labels. Additionally, we introduce a unified end-to-end training strategy to further improve efficiency of the framework. Experiments on multiple benchmarks show that Syn2DRE consistently outperforms prior state-of-the-art semi-supervised DocRE methods.

papers.title: A Spiking Neural Model of the Mental Lexicon: Representations, Similarity Structure, and Associative Retrieval in Perception and Production
papers.summary: A neural account of lexical access requires an explicit distinction between the structure of lexical representations, the associations linking representational levels, and the activity generated during retrieval. This paper specifies a spiking neural implementation of the mental lexicon within the Neural Engineering Framework and Semantic Pointer Architecture. Conceptual and phonological form representations are constructed recursively from relational graphs, whereas lemma representations provide independent lexical identities. The implementation contains 613 lexical entries and supports two directed processing pathways: perception maps a phonological form to its associated concept via a lemma, whereas production maps a concept to its associated phonological form via a lemma. Each pathway combines two associative-memory variants, winner-take-all (WTA) selection (competition) and thresholded transfer, and uses 199,400 leaky integrate-and-fire neurons. We formalize within-level similarity, cross-level associative retrieval, and the interpretation of decoded activity. Simulations show successful retrieval of eight selected words from the lexicon in both processing directions, with retrieval evaluated against all 613 lexical entries. These simulations use complete phonological forms as input for perception and complete concepts as input for production, illustrating lexical retrieval through the corresponding processing pathways. This paper provides a transparent description of lexical representations and neural retrieval mechanisms, supported by accessible code, lexical data, and online simulation documentation.

papers.title: An Effective Spoken Language Understanding Approach Leveraging Query-Adaptive Intent Detection
papers.summary: Large language models enable fine-tuning-free spoken language understanding (SLU) through in-context learning, but direct query-based retrieval may select semantically similar yet intent irrelevant demonstrations. This paper presents Query-Adaptive Intent Detection via Prototype Extraction (APEX), a two-stage retrieval framework that first selects candidate intents using intent-level prototypes and then retrieves contextual exemplars within the selected intent space. Experiments on the SLURP dataset evaluate joint SLU performance using Exact Match Accuracy (EMA) under full-transcript and perplexity-stratified conditions, with additional retrieval analysis on ASR-generated transcripts. Compared with query-based retrieval, APEX improves EMA by 4.34 and 3.97 percentage points with Qwen3 4B and Gemma-3-4B, respectively, on full transcripts. Under high-perplexity inputs, APEX also yields EMA gains of 7.66 and 2.13 percentage points. Retrieval analysis further indicates that prototype-guided candidate selection achieves higher ground truth intent coverage across multiple input conditions.
papers.title_zh: 一种利用查询自适应意图检测的有效口语理解方法
papers.abstract_zh: 大语言模型通过上下文学习实现了无需微调的口语理解（SLU），但直接基于查询的检索可能会选择语义相似但意图无关的示例。本文提出通过原型提取的查询自适应意图检测（Query-Adaptive Intent Detection via Prototype Extraction, APEX），一种两阶段检索框架，首先使用意图级原型选择候选意图，然后在所选意图空间内检索上下文示例。在 SLURP 数据集上的实验在完整转录文本和按困惑度分层条件下使用精确匹配准确率（Exact Match Accuracy, EMA）评估联合 SLU 性能，并对 ASR 生成的转录文本进行额外的检索分析。与基于查询的检索相比，在完整转录文本上，APEX 使用 Qwen3 4B 和 Gemma-3-4B 分别将 EMA 提高了 4.34 和 3.97 个百分点。在高困惑度输入下，APEX 还带来了 7.66 和 2.13 个百分点的 EMA 提升。检索分析进一步表明，原型引导的候选选择在多种输入条件下实现了更高的真实意图覆盖率。

papers.title: On the Effectiveness and Limitations of Open-Weight LLMs for Low-Resource Offensive Language Detection in Danish
papers.summary: We study the effectiveness and robustness of open-weight large language models (LLMs) for Danish offensive language detection, an underexplored low-resource task. We evaluate four model families (Llama, Mistral, Gemma, and Qwen) across eleven prompting strategies spanning five design categories, cross-prompt generalization, Danish orthographic variation, and robustness under balanced and naturally imbalanced class distributions. We compare against three BERT-family baselines with distinct pre-training strategies, evaluated via both masked language model prompting and supervised fine-tuning. Even without task-specific fine-tuning, LLMs can surpass all three fine-tuned BERT baselines, and lightweight finetuning yields substantial further gains. No single model or prompt category dominates, underscoring that prompt design interacts with model pre-training in ways that cannot be predicted a priori. Semantically grounded prompts transfer more robustly, while format-constrained patterns consistently fail to generalize. ASCII transliteration of Danish-specific characters (æ, ø, å) generally degrades performance, indicating these characters encode meaningful signal. At the same time, the gap between a balanced test set (best F1 of 0.84) and the corpus's natural class skew (0.62 trained on skewed data, 0.70 trained on balanced data) -- relative drops of 26.2\% and 16.7\% -- shows that class imbalance remains a critical open challenge. Our code and configurations are available at https://github.com/PASHAADC/Danish-LLM-HateSpeech.
papers.title_zh: 论开放权重LLM在丹麦语低资源攻击性语言检测中的有效性与局限性
papers.abstract_zh: 我们研究开放权重大语言模型（LLMs）在丹麦语攻击性语言检测这一尚未充分探索的低资源任务中的有效性与鲁棒性。我们在十一种提示策略上评估四个模型家族（Llama、Mistral、Gemma 和 Qwen），这些策略涵盖五个设计类别、跨提示泛化、丹麦语正字法变异，以及在平衡和自然不平衡类别分布下的鲁棒性。我们与三个具有不同预训练策略的 BERT 家族基线进行比较，并通过掩码语言模型提示和有监督微调两种方式进行评估。即使没有任务特定微调，LLMs 也能超过所有三个微调后的 BERT 基线，而轻量微调会带来进一步的显著收益。没有任何单一模型或提示类别占主导，这凸显出提示设计与模型预训练之间的交互方式无法先验预测。基于语义的提示迁移得更稳健，而受格式约束的模式始终无法泛化。丹麦语特有字符（æ、ø、å）的 ASCII 转写通常会降低性能，表明这些字符编码了有意义的信号。同时，平衡测试集（最佳 F1 为 0.84）与语料库自然类别偏斜（在偏斜数据上训练为 0.62，在平衡数据上训练为 0.70）之间的差距——相对下降分别为 26.2\% 和 16.7\%——表明类别不平衡仍然是一个关键的开放挑战。我们的代码和配置可在 https://github.com/PASHAADC/Danish-LLM-HateSpeech 获取。

papers.title: Benchmarking Speaker Embedders in the Sub-Second Regime for Real-Time Voice AI Agents
papers.summary: Real-time Voice AI agents must separate the active user from intelligible background speech that survives conventional noise suppression. Background sources include television audio, family members, and colleagues. Production denoisers remove non-stationary environmental noise effectively. Background speech shares the spectral characteristics of the target and passes through, causing false acceptances in downstream speaker verification (SV) and automatic speech recognition (ASR). We benchmark open-source speaker embedders TitaNet-Large, TitaNet-Small, ECAPA-TDNN, CAM++, and SpeakerNet under a strict sub-second latency budget. Evaluation combines a controlled benchmark with a weighted human-annotated production set. Our controlled benchmark is built from real calls in which a second real speaker is injected into silence intervals at modulated amplitude. We report three findings. First, denoising before embedding is generally harmful and raises equal error rate (EER) across architectures. Second, truncating audio below the full voice-activity segment degrades every model. Third, roughly half of the TitaNet embedding is redundant for this task. Trailing dimensions encode population attributes such as language and gender. Such attributes carry little discriminative value in a demographically homogeneous user base. We distill these results into deployment guidance. Verification should run on raw audio with full voice-activity chunks. Thresholds should favor precision over F1. Truncated embeddings reduce the cost of similarity search.

papers.title: Query-Guided RoPE Modulation for Lost-in-the-Middle Mitigation in Long-Context LLMs
papers.summary: Long-context language models often neglect information in the middle of the input, a phenomenon known as "lost-in-the-middle". Part of this gap may stem from the long-range decay of rotary position embedding (RoPE), which weakens the positional signal between distant tokens. Existing input compression deletes low-importance tokens, and attention reweighting acts only after RoPE has weakened this signal. RoPE-level methods modify positions directly but apply the same remapping to every query. To address these limitations, we propose QGPM (Query-Guided Positional Modulation), a training-free method that reshapes RoPE positions using query relevance from the model's own attention heads. QGPM builds a broad relevance map for lower layers and a sharp one for upper layers. Low-relevance tokens advance by less than one position on fast-rotating planes, pulling relevant evidence toward the query. Slow-rotating planes keep the original layout, with every token in place. Experiments on NoLiMa and RULER with multiple context lengths show that QGPM improves over base models and strong baselines, with the largest gains on retrieval tasks, and generalizes across multiple backbones. Our code is available at https://github.com/iZHpy/QGPM.

papers.title: RuACT: Recovering Inactive Rubrics as Adaptive Critics and Teachers
papers.summary: Rubric-based reinforcement learning (RL) extends RL with verifiable rewards to open-ended tasks by scoring each response against query-specific rubrics. Under group-relative optimization, however, a rubric that every sampled response fails (unreachable) or passes (saturated) gives all responses the same outcome and no learning signal; in Qwen3-4B medical training, 60.88% of query-rubric observations are inactive. We find that the two states lack different supervision: stating an unreachable rubric in the prompt raises its satisfaction from 1.13% to 91.25%, whereas responses that all pass a saturated rubric still differ in quality. We therefore propose RuACT (Rubrics as Adaptive Critics and Teachers), which assigns each inactive rubric the role that supplies what it lacks. Rubric as Teacher uses unreachable rubrics as privileged information for reward-gated on-policy self-distillation, and Rubric as Critic decomposes saturated rubrics into child rubrics that separate current responses while sharing the parent's weight. RuACT outperforms GRPO, rubric reweighting, and rubric-guided exploration on all four medical and scientific benchmarks with Qwen3-4B and achieves the best average with Qwen3-1.7B. On initially unreachable rubrics, unguided recovery rises from 35.02% to 42.86%, while child refinement improves reward-quality alignment on independent rollouts from 57.74% to 60.77%. Code is available at https://github.com/ZJU-REAL/RuACT.

papers.title: Steerable Multi-Objective Group-Relative Preference Optimization with Jointly Trained Low-Rank Adapters
papers.summary: Language model deployment often requires different trade-offs between competing objectives as user preferences change, yet standard post-training methods typically produce a single policy for a fixed objective weighting. We introduce LambdaMix, a new parameter efficient method for learning a preference conditioned family of policies with group-relative online reinforcement learning. LambdaMix jointly trains one low-rank adapter per objective over a frozen base model. One preference vector selects the adapter mixture that generates responses and weights the separately normalized rewards used to update the adapters. A single training run supports changing preferences at inference without further optimization. We experiment with four models on helpfulness and harmlessness and on solving math problems while following instructions. We also evaluate the two largest models on rewriting comments to preserve wording while reducing clues about personal attributes. On the first two tasks, LambdaMix achieves higher hypervolume than all evaluated conditioned and policy merging baselines across all four models. LambdaMix uses fewer training completions and stores fewer adapter parameters than a set of GRPO specialist policies. With architecture and initialization fixed, varying adapter mixtures and objective weights together gives wider score ranges and higher coverage than varying either alone.

papers.title: How Much Conversation History Does an AI Agent Need?
papers.summary: How does using less conversational history change reader-token use and benchmark scores? We examine this question on 1,100 BEAM questions. We held the retrieval ranking and reader constant across five fixed passage budgets, and mean assigned scores rose as the passage budget grew. The score gain per additional token became smaller at the upper tested budgets. Answerable questions generally received higher scores with more context. Pooled abstention scores sometimes rose as the passage budget shrank. We also tested message retention in a controlled task with explicit conversational-state targets and compared retained user messages with token-matched recency. Qwen matched the full state more often for direct requirements when user messages were retained. Its full-state matching declined when answers depended on references to earlier offers. Mistral produced near-floor results across the retention conditions. A scoring audit leaves the correctness of BEAM answers unresolved. These experiments characterize the token and score consequences of the tested memory budgets. Reliable budget selection depends on retaining the evidence each question requires and validating the measure used to assess answer quality.

papers.title: Language as Trait, Politeness as Strategy: Controlled Tests of Linguistic Effects in LLM Social-Deduction Agents
papers.summary: Large language model (LLM) agents coordinate through conversation, and the same message can be phrased in simpler or more complex language, bluntly or politely. We test whether such differences change how other agents judge and act, using the LURK Werewolf framework, which separates each utterance's speech-act predicate from its natural-language realization. We rewrite only the realization, check that the game content is preserved, and replay each game day from saved checkpoints against a re-sampled control. We vary linguistic range consistently across a speaker's messages and politeness strategy per utterance. Across 30 games and 4,335 replays, neither manipulation changes the trust other agents place in the speaker, and no effect on votes or night actions survives correction for multiple comparisons; the largest uncorrected effect is that shifting range away from a neutral paraphrase changes about 4 percentage points more of the other players' votes. In natural play, 88% of face-threatening speech is bald on-record regardless of role.
papers.title_zh: 语言作为特质，礼貌作为策略：LLM 社交推理智能体中语言效应的受控测试
papers.abstract_zh: 大型语言模型（LLM）智能体通过对话进行协调，而同一条消息可以用更简单或更复杂的语言、以直白或礼貌的方式表述。我们使用 LURK Werewolf 框架检验此类差异是否会改变其他智能体如何判断和行动，该框架将每句话的言语行为谓词与其自然语言实现分离。我们仅重写其自然语言实现，检查游戏内容得以保留，并从保存的检查点重放每个游戏日，与重新采样的对照组进行比较。我们在同一个说话者的各条消息中一致地改变语言范围，并逐句改变礼貌策略。在30局游戏和4,335次重放中，两种操纵均未改变其他智能体对说话者的信任，且没有任何对投票或夜间行动的影响在多重比较校正后仍然存在；最大的未校正效应是，将语言范围从中性复述移开会使其他玩家投票变化增加约4个百分点。在自然对局中，无论角色如何，88%的面子威胁言语都采用赤裸裸的公开策略（bald on-record）。

papers.title: ROSE: Risk-Aware Orthogonal Subspace Navigation for Lifelong Knowledge Editing in Multimodal Large Language Models
papers.summary: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) require continuous factual updates to stay current, yet lifelong knowledge editing remains a daunting challenge. The primary obstacle is the severe Locality Erosion and Catastrophic Forgetting, where sequential edits inevitably interfere with pre-trained capabilities and prior updates. In this paper, we propose \textbf{ROSE}, a \textbf{R}isk-aware \textbf{O}rthogonal \textbf{S}ubspace navigation framework for lifelong knowledge \textbf{E}diting. ROSE addresses forgetting by aiming to restrict parameter updates to the orthogonal complement of previously edited subspaces. Crucially, it introduces a risk-guided mechanism that utilizes a dynamically computed risk mask to safeguard specific factual parameter subspaces essential for model stability. During inference, ROSE employs a multi-granularity knowledge integration strategy, featuring prototype-anchored semantic gating and perturbation-driven subspace fusion to precisely activate edited knowledge for relevant queries while limiting interference on unrelated inputs. Comprehensive experiments on two prominent multimodal benchmarks show that ROSE is competitive with state-of-the-art approaches across five key metrics, while maintaining outstanding stability over $1,000$ sequential updates. Our code is available at https://github.com/sunlitsong/ROSE.
papers.title_zh: ROSE：用于多模态大语言模型中终身知识编辑的风险感知正交子空间导航
papers.abstract_zh: 多模态大语言模型（MLLMs）需要持续的事实更新以保持时效性，然而终身知识编辑仍然是一项艰巨的挑战。主要障碍是严重的局部性侵蚀（Locality Erosion）和灾难性遗忘（Catastrophic Forgetting），其中顺序编辑不可避免地会干扰预训练能力和先前的更新。本文提出 \textbf{ROSE}，一个用于终身知识编辑的风险感知正交子空间导航框架。ROSE 旨在通过将参数更新限制在先前编辑子空间的正交补空间中来应对遗忘。关键的是，它引入了一种风险引导机制，该机制利用动态计算的风险掩码来保护对模型稳定性至关重要的特定事实参数子空间。在推理过程中，ROSE 采用多粒度知识集成策略，具有原型锚定的语义门控和扰动驱动的子空间融合，以针对相关查询精确激活已编辑知识，同时限制对无关输入的干扰。在两个主流多模态基准上的综合实验表明，ROSE 在五项关键指标上与最先进方法相比具有竞争力，同时在超过 $1,000$ 次顺序更新中保持出色的稳定性。我们的代码可在 https://github.com/sunlitsong/ROSE 获取。

papers.title: Are These Programmers Ripe Enough to Eat? Evaluating How LLMs Handle Lexical Knowledge Conflicts in Translation
papers.summary: External lexical resources can help large language models (LLMs) translate texts in low-resource languages and specialized domains, but these resources may conflict with models' prior lexical knowledge. To isolate this conflict, we construct a controlled Mandarin-to-English translation task in which familiar source words are assigned new meanings within and across semantic categories. We treat these prompt-supplied meanings as contextual knowledge (CK) and systematically evaluate the effects of word frequency, sentence context, and prompt framing on the translated outputs. Across nine models, CK reliance is greater for less frequent source words and in sentence contexts that support the supplied meanings. Prompt framing can reduce CK reliance, but seven of nine models favor CK even when explicitly instructed to ignore the supplied meanings. Within model families, larger models are more likely than smaller models to utilize CK in their outputs. Three follow-up experiments further show that modal weakening lowers CK reliance, the effect of repetition depends on prompt layout, and the effect of reasoning varies across models. Overall, our controlled study reveals how CK reliance varies across conditions and models, motivating new methods to detect and evaluate lexical conflicts and guide models' lexical choices in LLM-based translation.
papers.title_zh: 这些程序员成熟到可以吃了吗？评估 LLM 如何处理翻译中的词汇知识冲突
papers.abstract_zh: 外部词汇资源可以帮助大语言模型（LLM）翻译低资源语言和专门领域的文本，但这些资源可能与模型先前的词汇知识相冲突。为了隔离这种冲突，我们构建了一个受控的普通话到英语翻译任务，其中熟悉的源词在语义类别内和跨语义类别被赋予新的含义。我们将这些由提示提供的含义视为上下文知识（CK），并系统评估词频、句子上下文和提示框架对翻译输出的影响。在九个模型中，对于频率较低的源词以及在支持所提供含义的句子上下文中，对 CK 的依赖更大。提示框架可以减少对 CK 的依赖，但九个模型中有七个即使在明确指示忽略所提供含义时仍偏向 CK。在模型家族内，较大的模型比较小的模型更可能在其输出中利用 CK。三个后续实验进一步表明，情态弱化会降低对 CK 的依赖，重复的效果取决于提示布局，而推理的效果因模型而异。总体而言，我们的受控研究揭示了 CK 依赖如何随条件和模型而变化，这激发了新方法，以检测和评估词汇冲突，并指导基于 LLM 的翻译中模型的词汇选择。

papers.title: Compaction, decay and reinforcement in a two-tier conversational memory: a paired evaluation against retrieval-augmented generation
papers.summary: A conversational agent that remembers has to decide what to keep. Retrieval-augmented generation keeps the transcript and searches it; the alternative is to compact each turn into atomic facts and search those. We compare the two on LoCoMo, with both arms answering all 1,985 questions in one window, against the same stores, with the same generator and judge, and both predictions on one row, which licenses McNemar's exact test on the 512 questions where they disagree. On the four categories comparable work reports, compaction scores 71.4 per cent against 64.6, a lead of 6.8 points (p = 5.5e-08) at 34 per cent fewer prompt tokens. On all five, including the adversarial set comparable work drops, the lead falls to 2.0 and stops being significant, because the baseline leads adversarial by 14.6. That loss has a structure. Our lead falls as the reference answer demands more source wording, 9.6 points ahead at one or two reference words and 3.1 behind past eight, with token overlap moving the same way, so the judge is not the cause. Compaction keeps what a fact asserts and discards how it was said, so it wins where the answer is a value and loses where it is a phrasing. We also report four negative results with their power calculations.

papers.title: CodeQuant2: Enhanced Outlier Mitigation and Adaptive Clustering for Low-Precision LRMs
papers.summary: Large reasoning models (LRMs) improve task performance by generating longer intermediate reasoning traces, but this substantially increases inference costs and makes low-precision quantization increasingly important. However, aggressively quantized models often perform poorly on reasoning tasks. We observe larger activation fluctuations during the first decoding steps of reasoning. Calibration that omits these early states may miss their activation fluctuations. To address these reasoning-specific quantization challenges, we propose \textbf{CodeQuant2}, a clustering-based LUT quantization framework for low-precision large reasoning models. CodeQuant2 mitigates activation outliers with rotation and scaling, uses clustering to represent non-uniform weight distributions, and adapts codebook sizes to the quantization difficulty of each layer. Guided by our observation of reasoning-time activation behavior, CodeQuant2 further improves calibration sample selection to better match actual decoding statistics. Combined with our customized LUT CUDA kernel, CodeQuant2 delivers substantial accuracy improvements on reasoning benchmarks while achieving up to $2.85\times$ speedup over BF16.

papers.title: AutoPYara: Next-Gen YARA Rule Generator for Malware Family Clustering
papers.summary: Millions of malware variants threaten users daily, such that clustering these samples is key for fast incident response. AutoYara is the current state-of-the-art for automatic YARA rule generation, but the task remains challenging on realistic datasets, where intra-family diversity and noisy clustering can degrade rule quality. We present AutoPYara, a solution armored with: (1) precise cluster centroid selection based on similarity hashing, and (2) an improved heuristic for estimating subclusters within a malware family using historical VirusTotal data. We implement AutoPYara as an open-source Python package (pip install autopyara) to support reproducibility and practical use. We show that AutoPYara, (1) increases rule coverage by 14 percentage points; (2) reduces variance by 7.1 percentage points, comparing the average variance AutoPYara exhibits to that of AutoYara; and (3) improves threat-hunting accuracy by 10%. AutoPYara produces robust and effective YARA rules than prior automatic approaches in practical settings.

papers.title: I Don't Care How You Hide It, I Care What You Do: Runtime Detection of Malicious ML Models
papers.summary: Pre-trained machine learning (ML) models shared through public platforms can be weaponized to execute malicious payloads during loading or inference. Existing scanners prove inadequate for detecting malicious models as they rely on static analysis and function denylists, support limited serialization formats, and miss attacks that replace denylisted functions with equivalent alternatives, exploit unsupported loading paths, or abuse legitimate framework APIs. To address this problem, we present ModelShield, the first runtime behavioral detection system for malicious ML models that attributes observed system-level behavior to specific model operations. It combines application-level instrumentation of ML framework APIs with eBPF-based syscall tracing, tracking model behavior across spawned threads and processes to separate model-triggered activity from environment noise. Attributed syscall sequences are classified using 195 detection patterns mapped to MITRE ATT&CK techniques. We implemented ModelShield to support 17 ML frameworks and 36 formats. On an independent dataset, it is the only evaluated tool to achieve zero false positives, with false negatives limited to payloads that produce no malicious runtime behavior. It detected all 29 published evasion variants spanning function substitution, loading-path obfuscation, and TensorFlow API abuse, where no existing scanner achieved complete coverage. Across 145,000 models scanned from public platforms, it captured 41 malicious models on Hugging Face, including a reverse-shell payload and a payload that performed host reconnaissance and outbound exfiltration. Among these, ModelScan, PickleScan, Fickling, and ModelAudit detected only 29%, 56%, 80%, and 93%, respectively. Despite runtime overhead, ModelShield has a median analysis time of 12.3 seconds, with 90% of scans completing within 35.5 seconds, making it practical for hub-scale screening.

papers.title: Conflux: Preventing Privilege Escalation with Principal Contexts and System-Level Evaluation
papers.summary: LLM agents combine information from multiple principals while acting externally. We formalise privilege escalation (PE) as the system-level security objective: an action may proceed only if every principal that influenced it would allow it. Model-level defences remain probabilistic, so enforcement must sit outside model judgement. We present Conflux, a principal-context defence. Its kernel, ITES, derives authority from provenance and the organisation's existing access-control system and intersects the permissions of every influencing principal. We prove a conditional authority-confinement theorem: under complete mediation, no-laundering provenance, a known non-empty decision context, fresh permission checks, and action binding, the kernel admits no action that escalates privilege with respect to any recorded influencing principal. The theorem covers the represented value-influence fragment; control influence from tool, branch, recipient, or plan-step selection remains a refinement obligation. Conflux extends the kernel with independent policy ports, argument-aware authorisation, disclosure, consent, delegation, restriction, and exposure planning. We describe two system- level evaluators. SLED is a black-box evaluator: it exhaustively explores a declared finite model of a defence up to a bound. SLED-V is a white-box evaluator: it checks a serialisable intermediate representation against security and provenance properties. The evidence is bounded and partial. The appendix reports retained AgentDojo, SLED, and SLED-V results, including the limits of those runs. No result in this paper is an unbounded deployment guarantee.

papers.title: Gain-Dependent Entropy Characterization of a Zener Avalanche Noise TRNG via Dual NIST Standards: Toward Low-Cost Hardware Entropy for ICS Deployments
papers.summary: True random number generators based on Zener avalanche noise offer a low-cost entropy source for industrial control system and IoT edge devices, yet the relationship between amplifier gain, coupling capacitance, and entropy quality remains uncharacterized under current NIST standards. This paper presents a comprehensive entropy assessment of an op-amp-based Zener avalanche noise generator across five gain configurations and two coupling capacitor values, evaluated against the NIST SP 800-22 statistical test suite and the SP~800-90B entropy source assessment using 1.44 billion raw bits per configuration. We identify a three-phase autocorrelation structure, attributed to comparator saturation-recovery dynamics, consistent across all gain settings. A direct-current substitution experiment, replacing the Zener diode with a stable voltage source at the same bias point, reduces switching activity by approximately 97%, confirming that Zener avalanche noise, rather than amplifier self-excitation, is the necessary entropy source. The coupling capacitor is further shown to govern comparator overdrive and entropy quality independent of this source mechanism, with the smaller capacitance improving entropy, throughput, and bias. The combined results identify an optimal gain configuration achieving a perfect statistical test score, NIST-compliant min-entropy, and peak entropy throughput at a bill-of-materials cost under five dollars, offering practical design guidance for low-cost entropy sources in industrial and embedded deployments.

papers.title: Jev as an LLM Safety Guardrail: An Empirical Study of Input Filtering, Selective Output Review, and Over-Refusal
papers.summary: External safety filters can prevent unsafe requests from reaching a large language model (LLM), but may also reject legitimate queries. We present an end-to-end empirical evaluation of Jev, a probabilistic decision model, as a safety guardrail for a Qwen2.5-1.5B-based pipeline. Three configurations are compared on 970 benchmark prompts: an unfiltered LLM, Jev input filtering, and tiered Jev input filtering with selective output review. Across 720 prompts labeled harmful (520 AdvBench and 200 XSTest-unsafe), the fraction recorded as answered decreases from 527/720 (73.2%) without filtering to 17/720 (2.4%) with input filtering. On 250 XSTest-safe prompts, however, non-answer/refusal increases from 3/250 (1.2%) to 27/250 (10.8%). Tiered filtering yields 40/720 (5.6%) harmful-prompt answers and 10/250 (4.0%) benign-prompt refusals, with 79/970 (8.1%) of prompts requiring output review.
